newsitem.title: USA: Compaq sees strong growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Compaq sees strong growth in 1997.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp, reporting higher 1996 fourth quarter results, said Wednesday it expects strong growth in 1997 and is in position to gain market share and increase profits.

Compaq reported fourth quarter earnings of $1.64 a share, up from $1.17 a year earlier excluding a non-recurring charge of $0.87 for purchased technology related to its acquisitions of NetWorth and Thomas-Conrad. Revenues rose 15 percent to $5.4 billion from $4.7 billion.
According to First Call, the Wall Street consensus estimate for Compaq's fourth quarter earnings was $1.53 a share.
For the year, Compaq reported worldwide sales of $18.1 billion, up 23 percent from $14.8 billion in 1995.
It said its gross profit margins grew to 24.4 percent in the fourth quarter.

"We expect strong growth throughout 1997," Chief Executive Officer Eckhard Pfeiffer said in a statement. "We enter 1997 with the strongest, broadest, most Internet-enabled and cost-effective product line in our history."
Compaq said it is focused on the high-growth segments of the industry with its Windows NT-based workstation line, an area forecast to grow over 40 percent by the year 2000.
